_comment: Hand-edited policy for the reference archive tool. Generated state lives in
the archive manifest, never here, so a re-run never conflicts with a human
decision. A fork changes 'depth' and re-renders offline.
Tracked paths whose URLs are another tool's WORKING DATA rather than
citations by this project. Harvesting them is not a boundary violation,
it is just wrong: a link ledger repeats every URL on the research page
with a health verdict attached, and a discovery-source list names feeds
to check rather than documents this project cites. Including them added
25 phantom references and a cited_by row pointing at a log file.
This is a path prefix list. It is not an exclusion RULE, because nothing
here is a judgement about a URL.

docs/references-md/ is the archive's OWN OUTPUT. Harvesting it would treat every link inside an archived article as a citation by this project, which is how a 519-reference inventory silently becomes thousands.
.claude/ and tools/ are this repository's own tooling. A URL in a skill's
reference notes, a dependency policy or the archive's own overrides file is
the tool's working data, not a source this project cites: they added Claude
documentation, a pandoc release page and the archive's own canonical-source
pin to the inventory.
Maintainer decision 2026-08-03: do not download binary media. A PDF, a
slide deck or a video can be opened at its own URL by whoever reads the
archive, and a local copy of a 30 MB deck earns little.
The cost, recorded rather than glossed over: if one of those sources goes
offline, the archive has the citation and the attribution but no content,
which is the exact case the archive exists for. This is a switch, not a
rule: set store_binaries true to preserve them instead.
Video is excluded on separate grounds anyway - the useful part is
metadata, description and captions, none of which is the media file.

ledger._comment: Optional and read-only. Absent, stale or schema-changed means 'no hint'.

host_aliases._comment: Only genuine host RENAMES belong here. Two hosts publishing the same article are a content-dedup question, not a URL identity one.
